filing_playbook.action: Conduct the required pre-application community meeting and post the 300-foot neighborhood notice as part of the CUA process, and respond to any neighbor questions about hours, trash, parking or noise.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: At the community meeting, present the operations plan, the hours (6 a.m. to midnight), the seating capacity (98), and the good-neighbor commitments (sidewalk maintenance, soundproofing, odor control, on-site trash, liaison officer). Answer questions about parking (none provided, rely on MUNI and street parking), delivery times (daytime only, no late-night truck noise), and trash pickup schedule (coordinate with Public Works for early-morning or mid-day service). Document all feedback and incorporate reasonable concerns into the CUA application.

timeline_cost.notes: This is the time to approval for the Conditional Use Authorization, building permit, DPH plan check and health permit when those approvals are granted. The Conditional Use Authorization is the critical path: 4 to 10 months from filing to Planning Commission hearing and 30-day appeal period. Building permit and DPH plan check run in parallel after the CUA is approved (14–120 days for building, 21–60 days for DPH plan check). Cost range covers the CUA application fee ($3,100–$15,000 depending on construction cost, with possible First Year Free waiver for new storefronts), building permit fees ($800–$15,000 as a percentage of construction valuation), DPH plan check ($828–$2,500 for a new restaurant, flat fee 8 hours at $276/hr), health permit to operate ($470 application), Fire Place of Assembly permit ($446), and FOG program registration ($0–$500). State and federal registrations (EIN, entity formation, seller's permit, EDD) add $70–$150 and take 1–14 days but are not counted in the approval timeline. Music licensing (ASCAP, BMI) adds $600–$5,000 annually and takes 1–7 days. The timeline assumes no appeal of the CUA, no discretionary review of the building permit, and no failed inspections; any of those add 2 to 6 months.

status_definitions.potential_blocker: Potential blocker: a cited rule, cap or record could stop this approval or force a change to the concept unless a specific condition is met.
status_definitions.not_permitted: Not permitted: a cited code section prohibits this use or approval at this address as the concept is described.
status_definitions.insufficient_information: Insufficient information: the records in hand do not show whether this approval is needed or obtainable; the could-not-establish section says what would settle it.

confidence_definitions.verified: Verified: stated directly by a cited record or code section that applies to this exact address, parcel or zoning district.
confidence_definitions.likely_applicable: Likely applicable: inferred from cited records of comparable cases or from a general rule; not stated for this address.
confidence_definitions.needs_confirmation: Needs confirmation: plausible but not supported by a record in hand; confirm with the agency or document named.
confidence_definitions.professional_review_required: Professional review required: depends on plans, an inspection, or legal or design judgment that public records cannot supply.

records_summary: The property at 243 West Portal Ave is in the West Portal NCD zoning district, where a restaurant on the first story is principally permitted without a conditional use authorization. The site history shows two 2012 Planning approvals for restaurant use with a Type 41 ABC license (beer and wine), indicating this address has operated as a restaurant. The immediate vicinity is densely developed with food and drink businesses: 11 registered businesses within 500 ft, including one bar, and 4 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 ft (Types 41, 42, and 48). Within 1,000 ft over the last 10 years, only 4 dated use decisions are on record for food/drink concepts, all approved (3 outright, 1 with conditions), with no denials—though the sample is too small to compute a statistically meaningful approval rate.
data_gaps: No hearing transcripts or staff reports available for the 2012 approvals at this address to confirm whether storefront merger or site-specific conditions were discussed.
The base rate sample (N=4) is too small to establish a statistically meaningful approval rate for restaurants in this corridor.
ABC license conditions for the four on-sale licenses within 500 ft are not exposed in the records; undue-concentration findings or operating conditions at those addresses are unknown.
The records do not show what 243 West Portal Ave is currently used as (no active ABC license on file); whether the space is vacant or occupied by a non-alcohol business is not established.

The 2019 conditioned approval at 36 West Portal does not state why 8 p.m. closing was imposed; whether it was due to residential proximity, applicant request, or neighborhood feedback is not in the extracted record.
